stem.en: A solution of compound B is saturated at 70 °C with 320 g in 100 g of water. It cools to 20 °C, where the solubility is 205 g per 100 g of water, and 115 g of solid comes out. What is in the beaker now?

text.en: 115 g of solid under pure water, because all the compound has come out.
320 g of solid, because everything dissolved comes out on cooling.
115 g of solid under a saturated solution that still holds 205 g.
115 g of solid under a solution that holds 320 g, because the amount dissolved stays the same.

explanation.en: 320 g went in. At 20 °C the water keeps 205 g dissolved, and the other 115 g is solid. The liquid above the solid is still saturated at 20 °C. It is not pure water: crystallization takes out only part of what was dissolved, which is why option a is wrong. Option d forgets that the 115 g came out of the 320 g. 205 + 115 = 320 is a good check.

hints.en: Add the solid and the dissolved amounts. They must come to 320 g.
What does the solubility of 205 g tell you about the liquid at 20 °C?
